items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: a representable morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S is a universal homeomorphism in the representable sense if and only if every base change Z x_Y X -> Z induces a homeomorphism of the underlying topological spaces (source lines 11100-11109). One direction is formal from the definition. The other uses the structure of universal homeomorphisms: from the representable sense one gets that X -> Y is integral, universally injective and surjective, hence universally closed by the integral morphism statement, so combining universal closedness, universal injectivity and surjectivity gives the homeomorphism property after every base change.
